text:
andrew: quick question — we keep running into correctness vs. sharing tradeoffs for prefix KV when two tenants share a slab. is anyone opposed to a small refactor that splits 'lease management' out of the slab owner and treats leases as first-class tokens?

linh: not opposed, but can you sketch the invariants we need to preserve? the main worry is stale reads if a lease is handed off but the old slab still serves cached entries briefly.

andrew: right. invariants I'm thinking: 1) a lease token L implies the slab will honor reads for prefixes in L until explicit demote. 2) when L is revoked, slab must stop serving any entry tagged with L after a fence epoch. 3) soft-evict should allow transient reads until kv-generation >= fence + grace_window.

sara: +1 to explicit tokens. curious about performance: will this require per-request token validation that kills hot-path?

andrew: good call. plan is token validation on cache miss path only (check residency table). hot-path (cache hit) keeps a small token tag byte per entry; eviction path scans check full token. so mostly zero cost.

mike: that still leaves shared-slab fairness concerns. if tenant A pins a prefix and tenant B floods, we need a backpressure signal that doesn't immediately hard-evict A. how do tokens express priority?

andrew: proposal: tokens carry a priority score and a credit-bucket id. eviction picks lowest effective score + credit deficit. token metadata is tiny (8 bytes) and stored in residency meta.

paloma: how do we handle migration? i.e., handoff from slab S1 to S2 during scaling — we need a handoff handshake to avoid RA/RW races.

andrew: handshake sketch: 1) new owner requests lease(R). 2) old owner transitions lease -> draining state and publishes fence_epoch + in-flight count. 3) new owner waits for in-flight==0 or timeout, then claims lease epoch+1. 4) old owner marks entries with fence and stops serving them.

linh: sounds reasonable. two followups: (a) what metric to signal rollout safety? (b) how to test racey path reliably?

andrew: for (a) we add metrics: lease_handoff_latency, lease_drain_inflight, served_after_fence_count. target is served_after_fence_count==0 in canary. for (b) I can write a small fault-injection harness that replays handoff with scatter of delays + network partitions.

sara: please add a compatibility shim: current API uses prefix_pin(true/false). map pin(true) -> lease with high priority token. pin(false) -> release. That keeps surface area small.

mike: and add a safety fallback: if new owner fails to stabilize in Xs, route reads to fallback model variant (slower but correct). we used that pattern in the model routing layer.

paloma: ops note — we'll need trace spans for handoff (trace.leases.handoff.start/finish) so SRE can correlate served_after_fence spikes to rollout.

andrew: agreed. I'll prepare a short RFC + canary plan: 1) token metadata in residency (no behavior change), 2) canary handoff experiments on dedicated small pool with opt-in, 3) instrument metrics & traces, 4) gradual roll to default slab allocator.

ci-bot: deploy queued: branch/kv-lease-tokens -> canary-evictpool (dry-run, no traffic)

linh: thanks. last nit — please include an escape hatch: admin API to forcibly revoke all leases on a slab (for emergency reclamation).

andrew: yup, admin revoke + audit log. I'll post RFC doc link shortly and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
